Anthropic 把 Claude Code 使用的沙箱运行时开源了，叫 sandbox-runtime。

macOS 用系统自带的 Seatbelt，Linux 用 bubblewrap，不需要额外启动完整容器，就能限制 Agent 对文件系统和网络的访问。

而且不只支持 Claude Code，自己的 Agent、MCP Server，甚至普通命令行程序都能用。

但这里有个很现实的问题：

Agent 写代码不只是改文件，还要装依赖、拉文档、访问 API。网络白名单收得太紧，任务可能跑不下去；放得太宽，沙箱的安全价值又会打折扣。

所以 Agent 沙箱真正难的，不只是把权限关起来，而是怎么在安全和可用性之间找到平衡。

もうAIの作業を画面の前で待つ時代じゃない。

posts.author: Akshay 🚀
posts.text:
4 types of LLM caching, clearly explained.

(KV, prefix, prompt, and semantic caching)

An agent can send the same system instructions, tool definitions, and conversation history on every turn. Without reuse, the model processes that shared context again.

That initial prompt processing is called prefill. It contributes to the wait before the first token appears.

The four caches in the graphic reduce repeated work at different points in this process.

𝟭) 𝗞𝗩 𝗰𝗮𝗰𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘀𝗮𝘃𝗲𝘀 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸 𝗯𝗲𝘁𝘄𝗲𝗲𝗻 𝗴𝗲𝗻𝗲𝗿𝗮𝘁𝗲𝗱 𝘁𝗼𝗸𝗲𝗻𝘀.

During generation, the model stores keys and values, the vectors attention uses to retrieve information from earlier tokens. Each new token reuses those vectors and adds its own, avoiding repeated computation at the cost of memory.

𝟮) 𝗣𝗿𝗲𝗳𝗶𝘅 𝗰𝗮𝗰𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝘀𝗮𝘃𝗲𝘀 𝘄𝗼𝗿𝗸 𝗮𝗰𝗿𝗼𝘀𝘀 𝗿𝗲𝗾𝘂𝗲𝘀𝘁𝘀.

When a request begins with an already processed sequence, the server can reuse its saved attention state and process the remaining suffix. This helps when requests share instructions, documents, or conversation history.

In vLLM, each cached block’s identifier incorporates the preceding prefix, so identical text after a changed prefix is insufficient for reuse.

𝟯) 𝗣𝗿𝗼𝗺𝗽𝘁 𝗰𝗮𝗰𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗽𝘂𝘁𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝘃𝗶𝗱𝗲𝗿 𝗶𝗻 𝗰𝗵𝗮𝗿𝗴𝗲.

A provider manages this prefix reuse through its API, including cache lifetimes and billing rules. Eligible repeated input receives discounted pricing, while the model still generates a fresh answer.

Put stable instructions and documents at the beginning, followed by the changing question, to preserve that reusable prefix.

𝟰) 𝗦𝗲𝗺𝗮𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗰 𝗰𝗮𝗰𝗵𝗶𝗻𝗴 𝗿𝗲𝘂𝘀𝗲𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗮𝗻𝘀𝘄𝗲𝗿 𝗶𝘁𝘀𝗲𝗹𝗳.

The system converts a prompt into an embedding, a numerical representation of its meaning, and searches for similar stored prompts. An accepted match returns the saved answer without calling the generation model, saving output tokens too.

This suits repeated questions with stable answers, but similarity alone cannot establish that an answer applies to the current user or situation.

These techniques can work together. A semantic cache miss can still benefit from a cached prompt prefix, then use KV caching during generation.

Prefix caching and provider prompt caching share the same underlying reuse. Semantic caching adds a different decision, whether a previous answer is still valid for this request.

That said, I also wrote a full breakdown of KV caching. The article is quoted below.

Hope you enjoyed reading.

Cheers! :)

posts.author: Xudong Han
posts.text:
Anthropic 最近开始建议企业「少用点 Subagent」，甚至把一些专家 Agent 重新合并回主 Agent Loop。

他们在多个企业项目中发现，单 Agent + Skills 的效果经常比复杂的多 Agent 架构更好。有个客户改成单 Loop 后，运行速度甚至快了约 2 倍。

原因很容易理解。

多个 Agent 之间反复交接任务，每次都要传递和总结 Context，信息容易丢失，延迟和成本也跟着增加。

Anthropic 现在更推荐让一个主 Agent 负责规划和执行，需要时再动态加载 Skills 和 Tools，把业务流程和领域知识留在可复用的组件里。

不过文章里有个细节值得关注。

他们曾把客服系统里的 Subagent 合并，延迟确实降低了，却让一个原本能完成的任务失败了，因为主 Agent 漏掉了向物流专家确认送达时间这一步。

所以作者强调，每合并一个 Subagent，都要用端到端 Eval 验证，尤其要检查哪些原本通过的任务突然失败了。

当然，并行研究、独立验证、Context 隔离这些场景，Subagent 依然有价值。

这样看来以后设计 Multi-Agent，可能得先问问自己，每个 Subagent 真的需要独立的 Context 和执行循环吗？

Anthropic 还开源了一套迁移工具，可以帮你分析现有架构，逐步合并 Subagent，并比较改动前后的质量、成本和延迟。很推荐做 Agent 工程的朋友试试。

CLAUDE + OBSIDIAN + LOOP ENGINEERING = A VAULT THAT RUNS ITSELF

the core idea: the vault is the loop's state, not the chat window

everything Claude Code remembers lives in a .md file - the Karpathy-style second brain, now wired to run itself

the loop:
> capture - a thought drops into 00-inbox
> context - Opus 5.5 pulls links, tags and nearby notes
> draft - Sonnet 5.5 edits inside a git worktree, never the live vault
> review - a Haiku 5.5 critic reads the diff before anything ships
> commit - appended to the vault, nothing gets rewritten

the key insight: frontmatter fields like supports, contradicts and supersedes are graph edges, not metadata

the note format itself is the write API. the second brain compounds on top of it

start with a plain loop. it runs about 2-4x a direct call

> switch to a full graph only when state has to outlive the session
> or when several agents need to coordinate
> or when you need to explain what changed
> that jump can run 10-50x

one review assistant walked from 55% to 72% to 84% just by climbing through these shapes in order

posts.author: Avi Chawla
posts.text:
6 KV cache quantization approaches, explained visually:

Quantizing model weights doesn't automatically shrink the KV cache.

The cache stores activations generated during inference, and its memory grows with retained tokens and concurrent requests.

KV quantization reduces the bytes used to store those activations.

For instance, moving from 16-bit to 8-bit halves the raw KV payload, before scales, metadata, and any high-precision buffers.

The diagram covers six approaches. In practice, several approaches can be combined within the same implementation.

1. FP8 cache

The KV cache normally stores each number using 16 bits. FP8 reduces this to 8 bits, so the numbers take up half the space.

A scaling factor adjusts their range before storage. The serving engine needs an attention kernel that supports this format.

2. INT8 / INT4 cache

These methods convert cached numbers into 8-bit or 4-bit integers.

INT4 uses less memory, but has fewer values to choose from, so rounding introduces more error.

During attention, the kernel converts the stored integers back into approximate versions of the original numbers.

3. Quantization granularity

Quantization uses a scale to convert numbers into a smaller format. One scale can serve the whole tensor, or separate scales can serve individual channels, tokens, or small groups.

Smaller groups fit their numbers more closely. But each group needs its own scale, which also takes memory.

4. KIVI-style quantization

Keys and values don't have the same pattern of large numbers, so KIVI compresses them differently.

For keys, it groups numbers from the same channel across tokens. For values, it groups numbers within each token. This helps preserve accuracy even at 2-bit precision, without fine-tuning the model.

5. Mixed precision

This approach keeps recent tokens' keys and values at higher precision and compresses older entries.

Attention reads both parts. Keeping some entries uncompressed avoids rounding errors for those entries, but uses more memory than compressing the entire cache.

6. Non-uniform / outlier-aware quantization

Uniform quantization rounds numbers to evenly spaced levels. Non-uniform quantization changes the spacing to better represent the numbers that matter.

Outlier-aware methods handle unusually large numbers separately. KVQuant stores these outliers in a separate structure, so they don't force the remaining numbers into a range that's too wide.

A smaller cache can fit longer contexts or more requests on the same GPU. It doesn't guarantee faster decoding, because compressing and reading the numbers also takes work.

Compare each method against an unquantized cache to check how much memory it saves, whether decoding gets faster or slower, and whether answer quality drops.

If you want to dive deeper, I wrote a KV Cache Engineering article covering quantization and other ways to reduce cache memory, with code examples and their trade-offs.

During this red-teaming exercise, we also found a vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution in Brotli, a widely-deployed compression library included in many pieces of software such as Node.js, Bun, and Envoy.

The flaw could let an attacker run their own code on affected systems by sending or replying with malicious compressed data, without any need to create a user account. That is, an unpatched server that accepts compressed input could be taken over by a malicious client, and an unpatched client that accepts compressed input (such as “curl --compressed”) could be taken over by a malicious server.

This root cause issue was actually fixed in the Brotli source code in February, but it wasn’t known at the time that it gave rise to a security vulnerability and there was no more recent release of Brotli. Since Brotli is built into other software, any software which includes this library needs to take the update too, followed by the users of that software. A Japanese student turned Claude Сode into a $10K/month bug-hunting machine.

his name is Kaito Yamamoto, a young security researcher who took 681 real bug reports and built something that feels like a tiny AI hacking team.

here's the crazy part. you can literally copy his entire setup for free:

companies pay security researchers to find vulnerabilities before someone else does.

instead of starting every hunt from zero, he built a system that already knows where to look, what patterns matter, and how to turn a real finding into a proper report.

and the numbers are ridiculous:

83 security skills. 15 commands. 681 disclosed bug patterns. 24 vulnerability classes.

all packed into Claude Code.

here's how the whole thing works:

-> INSTALL - add Claude-BugHunter to Claude Code from GitHub

-> PICK - choose a bug bounty program and an authorized target

-> SCAN - map the attack surface and identify the areas worth investigating

-> HUNT - Claude loads specialized skills for XSS, SQLi, SSRF, IDOR and other vulnerability classes

-> VERIFY - check suspicious findings, collect evidence and filter out false positives

-> REPORT - prepare a structured bug report for the program to review

-> EARN - if the program accepts an eligible vulnerability, you could receive a bounty

and here's what I find interesting.

the money isn't in telling Claude to "find bugs."

it's in building a repeatable process that turns thousands of places to look into a small list of findings worth a human researcher's time.

no magic money button. no guaranteed payouts.

just a serious security research workflow packaged into one open-source project.

GitHub: https://t.co/U9NnFVaR5Y

bookmark this. the repo has the installation guide, the skills and the full hunting workflow.
